inScope.answer:
Title: What a pattern (tul) is
Type: pattern
English: pattern
Korean: tul
Simple: A pattern is called tul (you may also see it spelled teul). It is a set of moves done in a fixed order, as if fighting pretend opponents. ITF Taekwon-Do has 24 patterns. Chon-Ji is the first one.
A pattern is called tul (you may also see it spelled teul). It is a set of moves done in a fixed order, as if fighting pretend opponents. ITF Taekwon-Do has 24 patterns. Chon-Ji is the first one.

Title: What Chon-Ji means
Type: pattern
English: The Heaven the Earth
Official ITF wording (source NZ-HB): Chon-Ji means literally “the Heaven the Earth”. It is, in the Orient, interpreted as the creation of the world or the beginning of human history, therefore, it is the initial pattern played by the beginner. This pattern consists of two similar parts; one to represent the Heaven and the other the Earth.
Simple: Chon is Heaven (the sky above) and Ji is Earth (the ground below). It is about how everything began, so it is the first pattern you learn. It has two halves that are alike: one for Heaven and one for Earth.

Title: How many moves Chon-Ji has
Type: pattern
English: 19
Simple: Chon-Ji has 19 moves. It is the pattern you need for the grading from 9th kup to 8th kup (yellow stripe to yellow belt).
Chon-Ji has 19 moves. It is the pattern you need for the grading from 9th kup to 8th kup (yellow stripe to yellow belt).

Title: Chon-Ji start position and diagram
Type: pattern
English: Parallel ready stance (narani junbi sogi)
Simple: Chon-Ji starts in parallel ready stance (narani junbi sogi). The floor pattern is a cross, like a plus sign. You stand in the middle facing D (the front). A is to your right, B is to your left and C is behind you.
Chon-Ji starts in parallel ready stance (narani junbi sogi). The floor pattern is a cross, like a plus sign. You stand in the middle facing D (the front). A is to your right, B is to your left and C is behind you.

Title: Chon-Ji moves 1 to 4
Type: pattern
English: Left walking stance to the left with a left forearm low block
1. Step the left foot to the left (B) into a left walking stance and do a low block with the left forearm.
2. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
3. Turn to the right (clockwise) towards A, into a right walking stance, and do a low block with the right forearm.
4. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: Moves 1 to 4:

Title: Chon-Ji moves 5 to 8
Type: pattern
English: A forearm low block in walking stance
5. Turn to face the front (D) with the left foot, into a left walking stance, and do a low block with the left forearm.
6. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
7. Turn to the right (clockwise) to face the back (C), into a right walking stance, and do a low block with the right forearm.
8. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: Moves 5 to 8:

Title: Chon-Ji moves 9 to 12
Type: pattern
English: L-stance (niunja sogi)
9. Move the left foot towards A into a right L-stance and do a middle block with the left inner forearm.
10. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
11. Turn clockwise towards B into a left L-stance and do a middle block with the right inner forearm.
12. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: The second part, the part for Earth, uses L-stance for the blocks.

Title: Chon-Ji moves 13 to 16
Type: pattern
English: The inner forearm
13. Move the left foot towards C into a right L-stance and do a middle block with the left inner forearm.
14. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
15. Turn clockwise towards D into a left L-stance and do a middle block with the right inner forearm.
16. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: In move 13 you block with the left inner forearm, and in move 15 with the right inner forearm.

Title: Chon-Ji moves 17 to 19 and the end
Type: pattern
English: Bring the left foot back to the ready position
17. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
18. Step backwards with the right foot into a left walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the left fist.
19. Step backwards with the left foot into a right walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the right fist.
End: bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.
Simple: At the end, bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.

Title: Punches in Chon-Ji (obverse punch)
Type: pattern
English: The hand on the same side as the front foot
Simple: All the punches in Chon-Ji are middle obverse punches (kaunde baro jirugi). Obverse means you punch with the hand on the same side as your front foot: right foot in front, right fist punches. A reverse punch (bandae jirugi) uses the other hand.

inScope.answer:
Title: Charyot (attention)
Type: command
English: attention
Korean: charyot
Simple: Charyot means attention. When you hear charyot, you stand up straight in attention stance, quiet and still, ready to listen.
Charyot means attention. When you hear charyot, you stand up straight in attention stance, quiet and still, ready to listen.

Title: Kyong ye (bow)
Type: command
English: bow
Korean: kyong ye
Simple: Kyong ye means bow. We bow to show respect, for example to the instructor, to a partner, and when we come into or leave the training hall.
Kyong ye means bow. We bow to show respect, for example to the instructor, to a partner, and when we come into or leave the training hall.

Title: Junbi (ready)
Type: command
English: ready
Korean: junbi

Title: Si jak (begin)
Type: command
English: begin or start
Korean: si jak
Simple: Si jak means begin, or start. It is the command to start the exercise or the pattern.

Title: Baro (return)
Type: command
English: return
Korean: baro
Simple: Baro means return. When you hear baro at the end of an exercise, you go back to your ready position.

Title: Kihap (yell)
Type: command
English: yell or shout
Korean: kihap

14. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.

English: Bring the left foot back to the ready position

19. Step backwards with the left foot into a right walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the right fist.
End: bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.
Simple: At the end, bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.

English: The hand on the same side as the front foot

English: The Heaven the Earth

8. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: Moves 5 to 8:

Type: pattern

9. Move the left foot towards A into a right L-stance and do a middle block with the left inner forearm.
10. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.

12. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.

Title: Chon-Ji moves 13 to 16

English: The inner forearm

14. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.

English: Bring the left foot back to the ready position
17. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
18. Step backwards with the right foot into a left walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the left fist.
19. Step backwards with the left foot into a right walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the right fist.
End: bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.
Simple: At the end, bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.

English: The hand on the same side as the front foot

Title: What a pattern (tul) is
Type: pattern
English: pattern
Korean: tul
Simple: A pattern is called tul (you may also see it spelled teul). It is a set of moves done in a fixed order, as if fighting pretend opponents. ITF Taekwon-Do has 24 patterns. Chon-Ji is the first one.

Title: What Chon-Ji means
Type: pattern
English: The Heaven the Earth
Official ITF wording (source NZ-HB): Chon-Ji means literally “the Heaven the Earth”. It is, in the Orient, interpreted as the creation of the world or the beginning of human history, therefore, it is the initial pattern played by the beginner. This pattern consists of two similar parts; one to represent the Heaven and the other the Earth.
Simple: Chon is Heaven (the sky above) and Ji is Earth (the ground below). It is about how everything began, so it is the first pattern you learn. It has two halves that are alike: one for Heaven and one for Earth.

Title: How many moves Chon-Ji has
Type: pattern
English: 19
Simple: Chon-Ji has 19 moves. It is the pattern you need for the grading from 9th kup to 8th kup (yellow stripe to yellow belt).

Title: Chon-Ji start position and diagram
Type: pattern
English: Parallel ready stance (narani junbi sogi)
Simple: Chon-Ji starts in parallel ready stance (narani junbi sogi). The floor pattern is a cross, like a plus sign. You stand in the middle facing D (the front). A is to your right, B is to your left and C is behind you.

Title: Chon-Ji moves 1 to 4
Type: pattern
English: Left walking stance to the left with a left forearm low block
1. Step the left foot to the left (B) into a left walking stance and do a low block with the left forearm.
2. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
3. Turn to the right (clockwise) towards A, into a right walking stance, and do a low block with the right forearm.
4. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: Moves 1 to 4:

Title: Chon-Ji moves 5 to 8
Type: pattern
English: A forearm low block in walking stance
5. Turn to face the front (D) with the left foot, into a left walking stance, and do a low block with the left forearm.
6. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
7. Turn to the right (clockwise) to face the back (C), into a right walking stance, and do a low block with the right forearm.
8. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: Moves 5 to 8:

Title: Chon-Ji moves 9 to 12
Type: pattern
English: L-stance (niunja sogi)
9. Move the left foot towards A into a right L-stance and do a middle block with the left inner forearm.
10. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
11. Turn clockwise towards B into a left L-stance and do a middle block with the right inner forearm.
12. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: The second part, the part for Earth, uses L-stance for the blocks.

Title: Chon-Ji moves 13 to 16
Type: pattern
English: The inner forearm
13. Move the left foot towards C into a right L-stance and do a middle block with the left inner forearm.
14. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
15. Turn clockwise towards D into a left L-stance and do a middle block with the right inner forearm.
16. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: In move 13 you block with the left inner forearm, and in move 15 with the right inner forearm.

Title: Chon-Ji moves 17 to 19 and the end
Type: pattern
English: Bring the left foot back to the ready position
17. Step forward with the right foot into a right walking stance and do a middle punch with the right fist.
18. Step backwards with the right foot into a left walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the left fist.
19. Step backwards with the left foot into a right walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the right fist.
End: bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.
Simple: At the end, bring the left foot back to parallel ready stance.

Title: Punches in Chon-Ji (obverse punch)
Type: pattern
English: The hand on the same side as the front foot
Simple: All the punches in Chon-Ji are middle obverse punches (kaunde baro jirugi). Obverse means you punch with the hand on the same side as your front foot: right foot in front, right fist punches. A reverse punch (bandae jirugi) uses the other hand.

Title: What Chon-Ji means
Type: pattern
English: The Heaven the Earth

It is, in the Orient, interpreted as the creation of the world or the beginning of human history, therefore, it is the initial pattern played by the beginner. Simple: Chon is Heaven (the sky above) and Ji is Earth (the ground below). It is about how everything began, so it is the first pattern you learn. It has two halves that are alike: one for Heaven and one for Earth.

English: 19

16. Step forward with the left foot into a left walking stance and do a middle punch with the left fist.
Simple: In move 13 you block with the left inner forearm, and in move 15 with the right inner forearm.

19. Step backwards with the left foot into a right walking stance, still facing D, and do a middle punch with the right fist.
